policy.support_rule: Required target support and current evidence are independent. Every policy cell remains blocking while current evidence is UNKNOWN, BLOCKED, BLOCKED_EXTERNAL, NOT_RUN, CONFIG_ONLY, WIRE_CODEC_ONLY, LOCAL_MODEL_ONLY, PROOF_ONLY, UNPINNED, STATIC_SOURCE, or ROUTED_GAP.
policy.version_rule: K1.2 names required semantic API keys and exact closure rules but records no numeric accepted range. K2.1 must freeze every reachable request and response schema, exact min/max version, header version, flexible threshold, broker floor and broker ceiling from independently admitted evidence.
policy.negotiation_rule: Each connection negotiates a broker/client intersection before ordinary traffic. Unsupported, missing, contradictory, stale, or reconnect-invalidated negotiation state fails closed; no local fuzz maximum becomes a production range.
policy.downgrade_rule: Fallback is allowed only when K2.1 names the exact fallback schema and K2.4 proves the transition is compatible. Silent version decrement, flexible-to-classic reinterpretation, security downgrade, and reuse of prior-connection negotiation state are forbidden.
policy.security_rule: Loopback plaintext remains accepted, remote plaintext remains refused, TLS verifies trust and hostname, and SASL exposes only SCRAM-SHA-256 or SCRAM-SHA-512 over TLS. SASL_PLAINTEXT is forbidden.
policy.credential_rule: Secrets are never emitted by Debug, Display, error, trace, receipt, argv, environment projection, or retained config. All owned and dependency-copied secret buffers require explicit disposition evidence; current static source inspection records only the narrow wrapper behavior stated here.
policy.negative_rule: Every negative trust, identity, credential, mechanism, proof, and downgrade cell must fail before broker-visible application effects, must be nonretryable unless the exact transport failure is classified separately, and must retain redacted diagnostics.
policy.unknown_rule: Unknown, blocked, unpinned, local-only, wire-only, config-only, compile-only, planned, proof-only, and silently skipped evidence never counts as support.

Any additional request or response API key reached by metadata, coordinator, idempotence, transaction, fetch, group, offset, security, telemetry, or recovery behavior becomes a required cell; absence from this minimum semantic set is never permission to omit it.
api_schema_closure.local_model_limitation: The checked fuzz target recognizes five keys and supplies synthetic maxima. It does not prove incumbent reachability, accepted production ranges, broker support, or response compatibility.

no_claim_boundaries: This K1.2 packet records only the exact checked-in static input pins, policy-cell inventory, required/current state separation, owner routing, source facts, and fail-closed disposition stated here.

It does not prove compilation, formatting, linting, tests, fuzzing, runtime execution, broker contact, container behavior, service health, network behavior, remote execution, or live RCH availability.
It records no accepted numeric broker or API-version range. The five local fuzz-model maxima are explicitly non-normative and cannot be cited as production support.

It does not prove Kafka request or response correctness, header selection, flexible encoding, unknown-tag behavior, negotiation, downgrade, correlation, reconnect recovery, stream reuse, broker interoperability, or oldest/current broker support.

It does not prove TLS trust or hostname verification, mTLS, SCRAM authentication, credential zeroization outside the narrow checked source wrappers, secret-safe native error handling, or any positive or negative real-broker security cell.

It does not prove actual native-library linkage or enabled SSL/SASL capability. Package-source expectations, mutable tags, ambient endpoints, config mappings, local models, proof declarations, and silently skipped tests are not execution receipts.

It does not prove delivery, idempotence, transaction atomicity, consumer-group ownership, offset durability, cancellation, shutdown, recovery, resource bounds, backpressure, performance, reliability, release readiness, broad workspace health, or absence of defects.
The minimum semantic API-key set does not close reachability. K2.1 must add every additional incumbent-reachable key and exact schema/range or remain blocking.
The packet does not authorize production wiring, shadow traffic, oracle retirement, dependency or feature removal, API or capability removal, file deletion, migration, or cutover.
